lessons.title: The Eval Harness: Auto-Testing Every AI Run

facts.text: The eval harness replays past sittings per lane, per class — a read-only replay gated on DELIVERABLE-PRESENCE, not exit code. oc-ds exited 0 with no deliverable twice when sandbox-blocked — exit 0 proves nothing.
The eval harness is the #1 next layer: it mechanizes the most-skipped layer (verification) and would have caught both live defects.

options: a lane can exit 0 with no deliverable

exercises.prompt: Why is the eval harness the #1 next layer?
options: it mechanizes the most-skipped layer (verification) and would've caught both defects

lessons.title: Quality Gates: Auto-Check Before You Ship

facts.text: Instrumented verification gates — a sitting won't close until exit + presence + class probe are recorded. Seam rule: gate logic stays a small script; past ~200 lines, stop and buy.

exercises.prompt: When does a sitting close under instrumented gates?
options: only after exit + presence + class probe are recorded
past ~200 lines of gate logic, stop and buy

exercises.prompt: The seam rule means verification gate logic should grow into a framework as it expands.

lessons.title: Skill Compounding: Turn Wins into Reusable Playbooks

facts.text: Skill compounding distills playbooks from the winning lanes' deliverable structure — but ONLY from ≥3 validated sittings per class, and only claims with confidence=verified + review_state=accepted feed it. Wrong lessons compound too, which is why the eval harness is sequenced BEFORE it.
The tightened rule: ≥3 validated sittings per class before distilling that class — 6 same-day sittings is overfitting territory.
Skill compounding reads ONLY confidence=verified + review_state=accepted claims — the hard filter against compounding unvalidated lessons.

exercises.prompt: A playbook may be distilled only after:
Why is skill compounding sequenced AFTER the eval harness?

lessons.title: The Multica Test: Why We Evaluated It, What We Kept

facts.text: The Multica evaluation REJECTED adoption on TWO gates: the license gate (condition 1b forbids removing/modifying displayed branding without a written waiver — the owner's exact plan) and the architecture gate (visible interactive board vs blind fanout; always-on = a re-platform trigger without a workload).

The corrected license reading (1a internal single-org use OK; 1b only protects displayed branding) opens the legal gate but changes nothing on architecture — the rejection was two gates, and the architecture one stands.

What survives from the evaluation: ideas only — board-as-metaphor for the ledger, agents-as-teammates framing for the lane inventory, skills-as-playbooks. The later integration landed in THIS workspace and is labeled owner-confirmed-current (evidence: the workspace itself), not blueprint-derived — the lesson teaches the evaluation AND the integration.

options: reject as an adoption, on license AND architecture gates
adopt the tool, reject the ideas

lessons.title: When to Rebuild vs. When to Extend

facts.text: Re-platform triggers are workload-shaped, not maturity-shaped: concurrent mutation of the ledger, always-on / event-driven (a daemon, not cron), and trust-boundary crossing (multi-user, per-user auth). Nothing on the roadmap approaches them — buy-verdict: nothing.
Adopting an orchestration framework now is re-platforming without a forcing trigger.

exercises.prompt: Which is a real re-platform trigger?

options: nothing — adopting now is re-platforming without a forcing trigger
